subject: Support access, limited transfers, and service-provider clause for US addendum
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@greencloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@greencloud.com, dpo@greencloud.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA addendum questions and support access

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Procurement and Legal are taking a pass at Redwood's DPA addendum for the US state privacy clauses (CPRA/CCPA). A couple of items came up we wanted to confirm before we proceed to internal approval:

- Can you confirm the classification Redwood uses for "service provider" vs "processor" in the US addendum? Our counsel wants explicit wording about limited use for contextual inference and no independent sale.
- We need clarity on support access: when our team opens an incident, what level of access do Redwood engineers get to customer data? Are support sessions logged, and can access be limited to pseudonymized telemetry rather than raw request payloads?
- Subprocessor disclosure: we asked for the latest list but would like assurance that any new subprocessor onboarding for telemetry/storage will require 30-day notice for our account.

I've attached a short list of questions our legal team compiled (GreenCloud_questions_0605.pdf). Let me know if you prefer a short call with procurement + DPO to resolve.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Procurement Manager, GreenCloud

---attachment: GreenCloud_questions_0605.pdf (pdf)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@greencloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA addendum questions and support access

Samantha —

Thanks for sending this over and for the good discussion yesterday. Short answers up front:

1) Classification: In our US addendum we take the "service provider" role per CPRA/CCPA language (limited use for providing services on your behalf). We can add an explicit sentence that prohibits "sale" and forward-only uses.

2) Support access: Redwood support engineers do NOT get blanket access to raw production prompts. Support access is time-bound and scoped:
   - Session-based access tokens with just-in-time elevation for troubleshooting
   - All sessions are logged with full audit trail (actor, timestamp, dataset accessed, justification)
   - Default telemetry exposed to support is pseudonymized by request id; full payload access requires explicit approval from your security contact or a signed escalation request.

3) Subprocessors: we maintain a public subprocessor list and provide 30-day notice for additions that affect telemetry/storage. For vendor onboarding that materially changes data flows we offer an onshore fallback plan where feasible.

I've attached our proposed redlines to the addendum (Redwood_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf). Can Marissa coordinate legal language and Karthik can add technical notes about telemetry handling. I'm happy to set a 30 minute alignment call if that would help.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

---attachment: Redwood_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@greencloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA addendum questions and support access

Samantha / team — quick technical addendum from infra side to support Grace's summary:

- Telemetry pseudonymization: for customer-facing telemetry we can hash or truncate identifiers at ingestion and persist only aggregated usage metrics by shard. This allows support to diagnose routing/latency without exposing prompt contents.
- If a support debug session requires payload-level context (e.g., reproducing a generation bug), we require a time-limited debug token that logs actor and full command, expires automatically, and is revoked after the session.
- KV cache and prefix caching are treated as ephemeral; we retain cache traces for 24 hours for debugging and then rotate. If your team requires shorter retention we can configure to 7 days or 0 days for sensitive customers (configurable per account).

Operational ask: can GreenCloud identify a single security contact who can approve payload-level debug sessions? That speeds incident response and keeps the audit trail tidy.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Platform Engineering
From: legal@greencloud.com <legal@greencloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: dpo@greencloud.com, samantha.lee@greencloud.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA addendum questions and support access

Hi Grace / Marissa —

Thanks for the redlines and the technical notes. A few follow-ups from our counsel:

- Please add express "no sale" language and a definition clause for "limited use" that includes examples (inference, model improvements only with our consent).
- For subprocessors, we need an account-specific commitment: 30-day notice for new subprocessors plus a right to object for material changes related to telemetry or storage.
- Support access: propose adding a sentence that any payload-level debug must be pre-approved by our DPO or by the security contact identified on a per-incident basis.
- We will need Redwood's SOC 2 Type II summary and the contact for escalation for support audits.

I've attached a short markup with questions for sections 2 and 5. If you can provide the SOC 2 link and the current subprocessor list, we'll aim to finalize next week.

Thanks,
Priya Kumar
Counsel, GreenCloud Legal

---attachment: GreenCloud_questions_0605.pdf (pdf)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: legal@greencloud.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA addendum questions and support access

Priya —

Appreciate the markup. We can accept the following edits and provide the references you requested:

- "No sale" clause: we will add a definition and explicit prohibition on selling Personal Information as defined by CPRA/CCPA.
- Account-specific subprocessors: we'll add a short clause that Redwood will provide 30 days' notice for onboarding subprocessors that affect telemetry/storage and will permit GreenCloud to object to material changes; if objection is raised, Redwood will engage on mitigation or provide an onshore fallback where feasible.
- Payload debug approval: we'll add that DPO or security contact approval is required for payload-level debug sessions and that every such session is logged with the originating ticket id and justification.

I've attached the current subprocessor list (subprocessor_list_202606.pdf) and a link to our SOC 2 summary: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/SOC2-report-2025. For audits, contact: compliance@redwood.ai.

Next steps: Grace — if you can confirm the security contact name, I'll incorporate the language into a v2 redline and send a DocuSign-ready copy.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. Our DPO (dpo@greencloud.com) will serve as the security contact for payload approvals. We'll review the updated redline once you push v2.

Timeline request: can Redwood provide the SOC 2 summary link and the v2 redline by close of business Wednesday (2026-06-10)? If so we can line up internal signoff and routing to procurement for DocuSign.

I'll also send a separate calendar invite for a 30-minute alignment if any open items remain.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Samantha
Procurement Manager, GreenCloud
